Impact & research

Evidence Strength Ladder
Download PDF guide

Research communication and impact prototype

Say what the evidence supports—no more, no less.

Place a research claim on a practical evidence ladder. See what can responsibly be said now, what still cannot be claimed, what evidence would strengthen the case, and how to write about it without turning activity or reach into proof of societal impact.

!
Evidence of activity is not automatically evidence of impact. A publication, dataset, media mention, event, download or positive comment may matter, but it does not alone demonstrate that research changed policy, practice, behaviour or wider outcomes.

Assess a claim

Add a precise claim and indicate evidence you currently hold. The tool recommends a conservative starting stage; reviewers should still check the conclusion.

Avoid adding causal language unless you have appropriate evidence for causation.

Evidence position

The current evidence supports an observed pattern or association.

      Interpretation safeguard

      This prototype is a responsible-communication and impact-planning aid. It does not assess research quality, prove causation, validate data, determine REF eligibility, or replace expert, ethical, legal, funder or institutional review. Any impact claim should be proportionate to the evidence and capable of credible corroboration.
